title: Elevate Telco Cloud Platforms with Core Network as a Service
gist: BCG argues telecom operators should industrialize cloud-native core networks via core network as a service (CNaaS) for standardized, low-differentiation functions. An IMS voice case study shows cloud-native cuts launch time ~50% and IMSaaS another ~30%, with IMSaaS TCO ~50% below self-deployed cloud-native at 1M subscribers but only ~10% at 5M, so the model favors smaller operators.

insights.claim: Core network as a service (CNaaS) extends telco cloud-native transformation by industrializing delivery: core network functions move from individually deployed and operated stacks to standardized, shared, managed services, ranging from single functions like IMS to dedicated IoT cores and full mobile cores.
insights.speaker: Michael Breitenstein
insights.so_what: Signals a new managed-service layer in telecom core networks; watch vendors and wholesale carriers packaging core functions as shared services.
insights.quote: shifting from individually deployed and operated core network functions toward standardized, shared services
insights.locator: We now see the first wave of operators exploring

insights.claim: Under CNaaS, the provider packages common infrastructure and carrier-grade platform capabilities (security, observability, automation, resilience) into a pre-integrated reusable telco cloud, leaving the operator to focus on network integration, service management, regulatory requirements, and migration.
insights.speaker: Michael Breitenstein
insights.so_what: Shifts operator spend from platform engineering and specialist ops toward service-layer work; reduces in-house cloud-native staffing needs.

insights.claim: Sharing infrastructure, platform engineering, and specialist operations across deployments lets operators spread fixed costs and scarce cloud-native telecom expertise, creating a repeatable foundation for deploying standardized services across markets and operators.
insights.speaker: Michael Breitenstein
insights.so_what: Talent scarcity in cloud-native telecom is a structural driver favoring shared providers with scale.
insights.quote: spread fixed costs and scarce cloud-native telecom expertise

insights.claim: Launching a shared CNaaS network function requires upfront agreement between operator and provider on governance (roadmap prioritization, upgrade scheduling, change approval), defined responsibilities, onboarding, incident and release management, and carrier-grade SLAs.
insights.speaker: Michael Breitenstein
insights.so_what: Governance and SLA terms are the friction point in CNaaS deals; contract complexity is an adoption risk to monitor.
insights.locator: Successfully launching a shared network function

insights.claim: BCG's CNaaS attractiveness framework rates services on two dimensions: degree of standardization and reuse potential, and potential service/market scale relative to the operator's internal capabilities to deploy and operate it independently.
insights.speaker: Michael Breitenstein
insights.so_what: Use as a screen for which telecom core services are likely to be outsourced versus kept in-house.

insights.claim: CNaaS fits best for standardized, low-differentiation services where service-specific scale or internal capabilities do not justify dedicated platform and operating resources — such as voice, IoT, and roaming, where reliability and compliance matter more than customized features.
insights.speaker: Michael Breitenstein
insights.so_what: Commodity telecom functions are the first candidates for outsourcing; differentiated services stay with operators.
insights.quote: The strongest CNaaS fit typically arises in settings involving standardized services, limited differentiation
insights.locator: The strongest CNaaS fit typically arises

insights.claim: Some providers that started with MVNO and IoT platforms are now expanding into IMS and 5G standalone packet core networks, showing CNaaS can move from niche functions to broader mobile services.
insights.speaker: Michael Breitenstein
insights.so_what: Track MVNO/IoT platform providers moving up-stack into 5G SA core as emerging competitors to traditional network vendors.
insights.locator: Some companies that initially focused on mobile virtual network operators

insights.claim: For small and medium-size operators, next CNaaS candidates include private enterprise networks, IoT and non-terrestrial network (NTN) use cases, roaming enablement, and Network API Gateway-as-a-Service; for large operators, contained use cases whose initial scale or uptake does not yet justify dedicated platforms.
insights.speaker: Michael Breitenstein
insights.so_what: Satellite/NTN and network-API exposure could be early managed-service markets, even at large operators testing new use cases.
insights.locator: Looking forward, this case study offers a path

insights.claim: IMS, the platform delivering voice over 4G/5G, is a CNaaS sweet spot because it is highly standardized with limited competitive differentiation, so reliability, regulatory compliance, low cost, and operational simplicity are the primary requirements.
insights.speaker: Michael Breitenstein
insights.so_what: Voice core is a commoditized function — expect operators to treat it as a cost line to minimize rather than a differentiator.
insights.quote: IMS is a sweet spot for CNaaS
insights.locator: IMS Is an Ideal Case Study

insights.claim: Moving from traditional IMS to operator-deployed cloud-native IMS cuts time to commercial readiness by roughly 50% via shorter design cycles, automated testing, and reusable test environments; IMSaaS removes roughly another 30% of implementation time through standardized designs and reusable integration assets.
insights.speaker: Michael Breitenstein
insights.so_what: Faster launch timelines strengthen the business case for managed voice platforms, especially for new market entries.
insights.locator: Following this speedier sourcing and contracting process

insights.claim: IMSaaS shortens sourcing and contracting because operators buy a pre-integrated managed service from a single accountable provider instead of coordinating IMS software, infrastructure, and integration across multiple vendors.
insights.speaker: Michael Breitenstein
insights.so_what: Single-throat-to-choke procurement threatens multi-vendor integration revenue pools.
insights.quote: procure a pre-integrated managed service from a single accountable service provider

insights.claim: Even though standardized IMS software can be provisioned within minutes, operator-specific network integration, testing, and certification still take longer and remain necessary before commercial readiness.
insights.speaker: Michael Breitenstein
insights.so_what: Integration and certification, not software, remain the bottleneck — limits how fast CNaaS can compress launch timelines.
insights.locator: Although telcos can provision standardized IMS software within minutes

themes.theme: IMS voice case study: cost and scale

insights.claim: Operator-deployed cloud-native IMS significantly lowers TCO versus traditional IMS, which relies on peak-load sizing, large capacity increments, active/standby reserves, and more manual life-cycle operations; the smaller hardware footprint gains value as memory and server costs rise.
insights.speaker: Michael Breitenstein
insights.so_what: Rising memory and server prices increase the payoff from cloud-native hardware efficiency in telecom.
insights.quote: The smaller hardware footprint becomes increasingly valuable as memory and broader server costs rise.

insights.claim: For an operator with 1 million subscribers, IMSaaS annualized five-year TCO per subscriber is about 50% lower than operator-deployed cloud-native IMS and 80% lower than traditional IMS.
insights.speaker: Michael Breitenstein
insights.so_what: Smaller operators have the strongest economic incentive to adopt managed voice core — a target market for CNaaS providers.
insights.locator: IMSaaS adds benefits by standardizing and sharing

insights.claim: The IMSaaS cost advantage shrinks with scale, from about 50% at 1 million subscribers to about 10% at 5 million, because self-deployed cloud-native IMS spreads build, integration, and hardware costs, gains licensing discounts, and lowers per-subscriber operating resources.
insights.speaker: Michael Breitenstein
insights.so_what: Large operators have weak cost reasons to outsource voice core; CNaaS addressable market skews to small/mid operators.
insights.locator: But the relative IMSaaS advantage shrinks

insights.claim: The strategic question for telecom operators is no longer whether to adopt cloud-native networks but which capabilities to build and operate internally versus source through standardized shared services.
insights.speaker: Michael Breitenstein
insights.so_what: Reframes telco capex debates toward make-vs-buy decisions on core functions.
insights.quote: The strategic question for most operators is no longer whether to adopt cloud-native networks

insights.claim: Operator-deployed solutions remain attractive where operators must keep direct control over established service scale, customization, sovereignty, and regulatory requirements.
insights.speaker: Michael Breitenstein
insights.so_what: Sovereignty and regulation cap CNaaS penetration among large incumbents.

insights.claim: Emerging commercial offerings and initial deployments show CNaaS extending toward comprehensive turnkey mobile core solutions supporting enhanced mobile broadband, beyond IMS, IoT core, MVNO/MVNE, private networks, NTN, and roaming.
insights.speaker: Michael Breitenstein
insights.so_what: If turnkey mobile cores mature, CNaaS could disrupt full core-network vendor relationships, not just niche functions.
insights.locator: CNaaS offers operators of all sizes an alternative

insights.claim: The IMSaaS analysis was informed by data and insights from Orange Wholesale and ng-voice, indicating these firms are active participants in managed cloud-native voice services.
insights.speaker: Michael Breitenstein
insights.so_what: Orange Wholesale and ng-voice are named reference players in the IMSaaS market.
insights.locator: BCG would like to thank Orange Wholesale and ng-voice
